meanings.note: Identity, profession or a characteristic; compare estar for a state or location.
A desire for a thing or an action.
Affection for a person, as in the lesson.
A state or location.
In estar bien or estar mal, evaluates an action or situation.

examples.text: No hace falta que lo diga.
examples.trans: There is no need for me to say it.

meanings.note: Transport something or someone.
With a duration, gives elapsed time continuing to the present.
Handle a client or their professional affairs; the agency use in this scene.

examples.trans: I've been here for two years.

examples.text: La agencia lleva a tres actores.

meanings.note: Move to a place.
With a gerund, presents an action developing over time.

examples.text: Poco a poco hemos ido mejorando.

meanings.note: Auxiliary before a past participle; does not express possession.
The impersonal present is hay, not ha.
Contact someone or call out to them.
The reflexive form llamarse gives a name.
Play a part on stage or on screen.
Behave or intervene in a situation.

examples.text: Mi hermana actúa en el teatro.
examples.trans: My sister acts in the theatre.

meanings.note: Tratar de + infinitive expresses an attempt.
Describes how a person is treated or a matter handled.

examples.text: Ella trata bien a la gente.

meanings.note: Possession, relationships and many fixed expressions.
Tener algo claro means to understand it or have a firm view of it.

examples.text: Tiene muy claro lo que quiere.
examples.trans: She is very clear about what she wants.

meanings.note: Common-gender person noun: el representante or la representante. Feminine in this lesson.
Informal praise. Masculine un crack is used for the female referent in this learner line, matching the corroborated audio. Feminine una crack is also attested; the adapted spelling crac also exists.

examples.text: Eres un crack con los números.

meanings.note: Todo el mundo means everyone and takes a singular verb.

examples.trans: I want to see the world.

meanings.note: Keep ñ: ano is a different word.

examples.trans: I've been here for two years.
This year I am working a lot.

meanings.note: For a person, el modelo or la modelo according to the referent. A model or example of something is masculine.
Changes to experta for a woman; the lesson uses the generic group plural expertos.

examples.trans: She is an expert on film.

meanings.note: Not the English exit; a way out is una salida.
Normally a singular collective in this meaning. The plural gentes exists, especially in other or literary uses; ordinary English people is not a reason to make the Spanish verb plural.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people.

meanings.note: The initial h is silent.
Before a noun it is a determiner; standing alone, todos/todas can mean everyone or all of them.
Marks many specific human direct objects without a separate English word; in poco a poco it belongs to the expression little by little.
Adverbial intensifier here; it does not change for the person who is loved.
Links a clause after a judgment in the first lesson example; introduces a relative clause about people in the second.

examples.trans: I'm looking for people who work here.

meanings.note: Subject pronoun; often omitted when the verb already identifies the person.
Unstressed direct object; can refer to a statement or idea rather than a masculine physical object.

examples.trans: It's difficult, but I can do it.
I want to go, but I am working.

meanings.note: Unstressed first-person singular object; its exact direct/indirect/reflexive role depends on the verb.
Stressed first-person singular pronoun after a preposition. Written with an accent, unlike possessive mi; may be doubled by unstressed me.
Más de introduces a numerical threshold; keep the written accent.

examples.text: Lleva más de un año aquí.
examples.trans: She has been here for more than a year.

meanings.note: Also links tratar de + infinitive and forms more than with más de; these uses do not express possession.

examples.text: Llevo más de dos años aquí.
examples.trans: I've been here for more than two years.

meanings.note: Written as one word; no accent mark in this number.
In poco a poco, the two occurrences belong to one expression meaning gradually.

examples.trans: Little by little, I'm understanding it.

meanings.note: The choice after experto is en; English may use at, in or on according to the following activity or subject.

examples.trans: She is an expert on film.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, reinforces the present time without agreeing with a person.
A standalone answer can precede a separate negative statement, producing two occurrences of no.
Introduces a role or a comparison. No written accent in this use; the question word cómo is different.
Neuter demonstrative for a thing, situation or idea; no plural and no noun directly after it.
Understandable, evident, or settled in someone's mind in tener algo claro.
In farewell expressions, introduces the next meeting; do not translate the farewell word for word.
Source-attested name or surname. Name history is supplied separately with its own evidence and uncertainty; no unverified full name is inferred.
